rationale: Vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; low discontinuation syndrome risk) to sertraline (SSRI; t½ ~26h; moderate discontinuation syndrome risk). Vortioxetine's long half-life provides a natural self-taper. Direct switch is clinically reasonable. Sertraline is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor — but since vortioxetine will be stopped, this interaction is not clinically relevant here (sertraline does not require vortioxetine dose adjustment when used as a replacement). Brief overlap acceptable. Both drugs are serotonergic — standard low serotonin syndrome risk at therapeutic doses. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Stop vortioxetine. Start sertraline 50 mg. Vortioxetine residual plasma levels will persist for ~10–14 days but at declining sub-therapeutic concentrations. Sertraline is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor — this may theoretically slow vortioxetine clearance slightly during washout but is not clinically significant.
Vortioxetine cleared. Continue sertraline 50 mg. Titrate to 100 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Vortioxetine 20 mg → sertraline 50 mg (standard effective doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
